source.name: Tabbing past the last visible control of a modal must wrap inside the modal even when it contains hidden buttons
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/ghosh/micromodal/issues/295) at 777dbcbeaf6314da0a3669f2b5ed9cdd66e6fc8a. Blind to the maintainers' fix 70dfd4320d9e0e535be432f57c698c75e230d0b3; routing auto.

journey.title: Tab stays inside the upload dialog when it contains a hidden button
journey.goal: Tabbing past the last visible control wraps to the start of the dialog

steps.title: Tab past the last visible control

functionalJourney.title: Upload a report with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: The dialog opens, uploads and closes

guards.title: Escape closes the upload dialog and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: The visually hidden retry button remained focusable according to Micromodal's focusable node list (due to matching selectors despite CSS display:none), causing the script to treat it as a focusable element after the Upload button. Consequently, the Tab keypress from Upload did not trigger the focus‑wrapping logic, allowing focus to escape the modal to the Help link outside.
plan.repair_strategy: Add aria-hidden="true" to the retry button so that Micromodal's getFocusableNodes excludes it, aligning the script's focusable set with the browser's actual tab order. This makes the Upload button the last focusable element inside the dialog, enabling the existing focus‑wrapping behavior to move focus back to the first element (Close button) on Tab.

edits.before:
<button id="upload" type="button">Upload</button>
      <button id="retry" class="retry" type="button">Try again</button>
edits.after:
<button id="upload" type="button">Upload</button>
      <button id="retry" class="retry" type="button" aria-hidden="true">Try again</button>

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will remain trapped within the modal when tabbing forward, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order). The modal’s focus order will be: Open button → File name input → Upload button → Close button → (wrap).
functional_risks: None; the button remains visually hidden and non‑functional, so adding aria-hidden does not affect appearance or any existing functionality.
verification_requirements: After opening the modal, pressing Tab moves focus from #filename to #upload.
Pressing Tab again moves focus from #upload to #modal-close.
Escape key still closes the modal and returns focus to the trigger button.
Status text updates correctly after an upload action.
No regression in other modal interactions (e.g., Shift+Tab works as expected).
